title: Younger Dryas cold interval
summary: The Younger Dryas was an abrupt return to near-glacial conditions that began about 12,800 years ago and ended about 11,600 years ago. It is best seen in Greenland ice cores, with effects reaching Europe and North America. Its cause is debated, with freshwater input to the North Atlantic the leading idea; effects varied by region, with little response in some tropical records.

uncertainty.note: Dated in years before present; Greenland records give roughly 12.8 to 11.6 thousand years ago and a tropical stalagmite 12.92 and 11.36 thousand years ago, counted from 1950.

where.modern_name: Greenland, used as a marker only; a hemispheric to global climate event
where.historical_name: No single place; strongest signal in the North Atlantic region and Greenland

importance.justification: The last abrupt cold event of the glacial period, widely used as a reference point for rapid climate change.
